newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil edge up on firmer crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil edge up on firmer crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged up slightly in quiet trading on Monday over firmer crude values in the absence of fresh indicators, traders said.
"Gas oil sentiment improved slightly because of crude but the fundamentals are still the same--there is a lot of oil out there," one trader said.
August swaps were indicated at $21.00/$21.20 per barrel, up from Friday's $20.95/$21.05. August traded to a high of $20.05 late Friday, brokers said.
September was quoted at $22.00/$22.20, also up about five cents from Friday with the August/September spread firmly established at minus $1.00 per barrel value.
On Friday, August Brent crude closed up 13 cents to end at $18.09 on London's International Petroleum Exchange.
Traders said gas oil remains under pressure as sellers offered cargoes at repeatedly lower prices throughout last week in an effort to get rid of prompt cargoes.

On Friday a 30,000 tonne cargo was offered at $148.50 per tonne ($19.93 per barrel) and a 150,000 barrel cargo at $20.00--the lower offer being the first time in over three years that gas oil was offered below the $20.00 mark.
Although a buyer emerged for these cargoes but no deal was struck as the two parties could not agree on terms.
Traders said they expect similar offers to made later Monday which will continue to weigh down on prices in the absence of fresh regional demand.
The regrade remains well supported despite strong selling pressure on the physical jet market due to bigger falls to gas oil values, traders said.
August regrade was valued at about $1.90 per barrel unchanged from Friday.
Fuel oil swaps were quoted lower as buyers were reluctant to raise their bids with sellers holding their offers steady.
August and September were last quoted at $98.00/$99.00, down from Friday's $98.50/$99.00.
